chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

For a Muslim upon his Muslim brother, from the rights, is that he greets him when he meets him, and visits him when he is sick, and advises him when he is absent, and says 'Yarhamuk Allah' when he sneezes, and answers him when he invites him, and follows him (in funeral) when he dies.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, similar to it.

key_terms.يُسَمِّتَهُ: Says 'Yarhamuk Allah' (May Allah have mercy on you) upon sneezing

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a Muslim upon his Muslim brother according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi’s chapter on the rights of the believer, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies the social bonds of Islam into actionable duties, ranging from public greetings to private counsel. It reflects the Shia emphasis on 'Huquq al-Ikhwa' (rights of brotherhood) as a means of strengthening communal cohesion and spiritual purity. The inclusion of 'advising in absence' highlights the importance of sincerity and trustworthiness in the community's moral fabric.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘For a Muslim upon his Muslim brother, from the rights is that he greets him when he meets him, and consoles him when when sick, and advises for him when absent, and Name (say May Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Bless you) when he sneezes, and answer him when he invites him, and follow him (his funeral) when he dies’.
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba – similar to it.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Of the rights of Muslin on a Muslim is to offer him the greeting of peace upon meeting him, visit him when he is ill, protect his interest when he is absent, say, ‘May Allah bless you’ when he sneezes, accept his invitation and take part in the procession for his funeral.”
A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah a similar Hadith.
